summary: MODEL_CHANGE_REQUIRED: the update adds an optional Pre-Vote round. The reference, MC, Trace, and harness were updated (plus repairs of pre-existing model defects), 21 fresh traces validate, and model checking found two update-introduced defects, both reproduced through the public Raft API: stale Pre-Vote responses from an earlier round are counted (RaftCore panics when the responder was removed), and a Pre-Vote round started while Candidate survives leader establishment so the new Leader re-elects.
validation_limits: Bounded three-node model (MaxTerm 2, MaxLogIndex 4, bounded election/membership/crash/drop counters and message bag); 30-minute BFS runs did not exhaust their queues and simulations are sampled (spec/output/campaigns.md).
Model time is abstract: tick restarts and response delays are unconstrained; reachability of each finding was confirmed in code (spec/confirmation-MC-1.md, spec/confirmation-MC-2.md).
Follower-side membership replication and the leadership-transfer lease bypass are not modeled (V0 abstractions kept); the MC-1 panic is reached through leader-side membership change.
Engine-level traces cannot observe the RaftCore Pre-Vote response filter; it is exercised by the integration reproduction.
Old-revision controls are not applicable: the old revision has no Pre-Vote round or Trigger::elect(bool).

findings.title: Pre-Vote responses of an earlier round are accepted by a later round of the same term
findings.cause: Engine::pre_elect builds every round from the unchanged local vote, so all rounds at one local term share the leader id (term+1, self); RaftCore::does_pre_candidate_vote_match compares only leader ids, and Candidate::grant_by expects the responder to be a voter of the current round.
findings.trigger: A node starts a Pre-Vote round, starts another round at the same term (timer restart, trigger().elect(true), or after leader contact dropped the first), and a granted response to the first round arrives; for the panic, the responder was removed from the voter set between the rounds.
findings.consequence: The grant is tallied by the wrong round: RaftCore panics (Fatal::Panicked) when the responder is no longer a voter, and otherwise a real election can start on grants the current round never received, inflating the term.

premises: Two Pre-Vote rounds of one node can start at the same local term (timer restart after election_timeout, operator trigger().elect(true) without rate limit, or a new round after become_following dropped one).
A granted response to the earlier round can be processed after the later round started (within the RPC ttl election_timeout_min, or queued as a notification).
For the panic consequence, the responder is removed from the voter set between the rounds.

findings.title: A Pre-Vote round started while Candidate survives leader establishment; the new Leader starts another election
findings.cause: The election timer (and trigger().elect(true)) runs pre_elect for a Candidate without cancelling its election; establish_leader does not drop Engine.pre_candidate, and handle_pre_vote_resp calls elect() on quorum without checking the node's role, leaving a stale leader object.
findings.trigger: A Candidate starts a Pre-Vote round while its real election is in flight; the real election wins, then the Pre-Vote grants arrive.
findings.consequence: The freshly established Leader steps down and starts an election at term+1 (term inflation, leadership loss); in debug builds RaftCore panics on try_leader_handler's assertion leader.vote >= state.vote.

premises: The election timer keeps firing for a Candidate and, with enable_pre_vote, runs pre_elect without cancelling the running election (or an operator calls trigger().elect(true) on a Candidate).

The real election reaches quorum before the Pre-Vote grants are processed (timer path: needs vote replies delayed beyond election_timeout but within the RPC ttl or queued; operator path: no timing constraint).

findings.title: Pre-Vote backward-compatibility documentation contradicts the default pre_vote and grant counting
findings.cause: docs/protocol/pre_vote.md says the default pre_vote returns Unreachable and Unreachable counts as a grant; the code returns a granted response and never counts transport errors.
findings.trigger: Reading the protocol document for a mixed-version cluster.
findings.consequence: No behavioral consequence: code, code comments, and tests agree; only the document is stale.
